_what: Measured leg-to-leg coefficient of variation, per scene, per key, in PERCENT. This is the noise a comparison must clear before it means anything. Consumed by scripts/leg-diff.py.
_provenance: docs/evidence/scene-stability.md -- 12 legs, 4 scenes x 3 passes interleaved by pass, 90s each, asset chain 6f763c36bbb38e08, 2026-08-22. Derived from three legs per scene: these RANK scenes and size a floor, they do not certify one. Re-measure with more legs before treating any figure as precise.
_renamed_2026_08_22: Scene keys are now the HYPHENATED bookmark names, which is what the harness records and what leg-diff looks up. Two of them were previously keyed with SPACES ('01 Lava Refinery', '03 Surface Outpost') while the bookmarks, the logs and the evidence doc all used hyphens -- so both floors were correctly measured and NEITHER COULD EVER BE FOUND, and leg-diff would have refused at those scenes citing 'no measured floor' while the measurement sat here. The bookmarks in the harness save were themselves standardised to hyphens in the same change, so there is now one spelling rather than a convention. THESE ARE RELABELS, NOT RE-MEASUREMENTS: every number above is the same number, from the same legs, for the same physical place.
_how_to_use: For an UNPAIRED comparison of na vs nb legs the difference has sd = cv*sqrt(1/na + 1/nb); a two-sided 95% bar is 1.96x that. leg-diff.py applies it. A PAIRED comparison removes the between-leg component and is not bound by this floor -- which is the whole reason to pair.

_insensitive.cpu.frame.total.us: PACING-BOUND, NOT PRECISE. Its CV reads 0.004-0.098%, which is not stability -- the key is largely vsync sleep, so it barely moves however the engine performs. A floor that small would let any difference clear it, which is a check that cannot fail. leg-diff.py REFUSES to attribute on keys listed here regardless of their measured floor. The trap is already recorded at scripts/telemetry-window.py's cpu.frame.total.us note and in [#173]: a total that is 65% sleep reports no change for a real regression.

_fixtures_what: A floor is keyed on WHERE **and WHAT THE PLAYER IS DOING**. `scenes` above holds the STILL floors -- the player standing motionless -- and that is the default a leg gets when its artefact records no motion fixture. A leg driven by STAR_RENDERTEST_WALK ([#174]) is a DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT of the same place: walking costs ~23% more render CPU than standing at 04-Ocean-Factory (docs/evidence/walking-fixture.md), so a standing bar applied to a moving leg is the same basis mismatch as [#285]. leg-diff.py therefore reads meta.walk off each leg, REFUSES to compare across fixtures, and looks the floor up under `fixtures.<name>.<scene>` with NO FALLBACK to the still entry -- a fixture without its own measured floor refuses rather than borrowing a wrong one.

_fixtures_provenance.walk/04-Ocean-Factory: MEASURED 2026-08-22 for [#286]: STAR_RENDERTEST_WALK=45, 4 legs of 90s, warm-up discarded, n=3, asset chain 6f763c36bbb38e08. Derived through leg-diff's OWN loader, so the basis that applies these floors is the basis that produced them -- which is the [#285] discipline applied at the point of measurement rather than discovered afterwards. THE LEGS ASSERT THEIR OWN FIXTURE: each artefact carries meta.walk=45, written by the profiler. An EARLIER bank of four walking legs existed but predated that wiring, so it self-reported `still`; rather than backfill the field by hand -- which would make my say-so, not the artefact, the evidence -- the four legs were re-run. WALKING IS STEADIER THAN STANDING HERE, which was not the expected direction: lighting.cpu.total.us 6.37% against the still 13.95%, cpu.frame.render.us 5.74% against 8.95%, cpu_cost 3.53% against 3.61%. Only lighting.produce.entities.us is worse (10.16% against 7.37%), which is the one key whose content genuinely moves. So the moving fixture is not a noisier instrument than the standing one; at this scene it is a better one, and [#274]'s border lever -- unresolvable standing, because its effect is smaller than the still fixture's own 13.95% noise -- may be resolvable unpaired here.
_fixtures_provenance._n3_DOES_NOT_PIN_A_CV: AND THE DISCARDED BANK IS EVIDENCE, NOT WASTE. The earlier four legs were the same binary at the same scene on the same fixture, and their CVs disagree with the recorded ones by up to 3.8x: produce.entities 19.60 vs 10.16, drive.point 11.03 vs 2.88, cpu_cost 10.72 vs 3.53, union 7.27 vs 4.75, and lighting.cpu.total moves the other way at 5.44 vs 6.37. TWO INDEPENDENT n=3 BANKS OF THE SAME THING DO NOT AGREE ON THE NOISE. A floor derived from three legs is a usable REFUSAL THRESHOLD -- which is all leg-diff asks of it -- but it is not a precise figure and must never be quoted as one, here or in the `scenes` table above, which is derived the same way. This is [#268]'s finding arriving from a second direction: the whole-CPU keys are drift-bound, and a between-bank component exists that a within-bank spread cannot see.
_fixtures_provenance._still_settling_is_present_here_too: cpu.frame.render.us falls 2562.4 -> 2369.4 -> 2294.6 across the three legs, the same monotonic settle the still floors carry at this scene and the ship. A residual trend is being counted as noise, so every figure above is PESSIMISTIC by an unmeasured amount.

_warmup.03-Surface-Outpost: cpu_cost ran 611 -> 560 -> 216 us/frame across three visits, ~3x monotonic. Its floors above INCLUDE that transient and are therefore pessimistic. Discard a warm-up leg at this scene.
_warmup.00-Ocean-Lab: p1 high then settles; post-transient its cpu_cost spread falls to 0.90% and render to 5.25%, both better than Desert-Town. The candidate second scene ([#242]), once its warm-up is discarded and its own repeat count established.
_warmup.Desert-Town: no transient observed across three passes.
_warmup.04-Ocean-Factory: MEASURED 2026-08-22, 1 warm-up discarded + 3 legs, as the prerequisite for [#274]. AND IT SETTLES THE METHOD BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT: lighting.cpu.total.us -- the exact key [#217] measured its -10.1% border lever on -- has an UNPAIRED CV of 13.95%. The effect being re-derived is SMALLER THAN THIS SCENE'S OWN UNPAIRED NOISE. So an unpaired A/B here cannot resolve it at any repeat count that matters: the bar is 1.96*cv*sqrt(1/na+1/nb), and at n=4 per arm that is still ~19%. ONLY A PAIRED DESIGN CAN ANSWER [#274], which is what scripts/render-ab.sh was built for ([#279]) -- pairing removes the between-leg component this floor is made of. Do not read the -10.1% as refuted by this; read it as unresolvable by the unpaired method. Also carries the same residual settling trend as the ship: cpu.frame.render.us falls 2423.5 -> 2140.6 -> 2044.3 across the three legs, so this floor is PESSIMISTIC by an unmeasured amount.
_warmup.ship: ONE DISCARDED WARM-UP LEG WAS NOT ENOUGH HERE. The three legs behind the floor above still fall monotonically -- render 1951.8 -> 1778.9 -> 1726.2, cpu_cost 477.5 -> 433.9 -> 413.2 -- so a residual settling trend is being counted as noise and every ship floor above is PESSIMISTIC by an unmeasured amount. It is a usable refusal threshold, which is what a floor is for, but it is not the ship's true leg-to-leg spread and must not be quoted as one. Re-derive from the cartesian's ship baselines, which have more legs after a longer settle.

_derived_key_floors: lighting.cpu.union.us is DERIVED, not registered -- leg-diff synthesises it per leg from the gated membership ([#281], [#283]). A derived key gets no floor for free, so this one was measured 2026-08-22 from the SAME banked legs behind every other 04-Ocean-Factory figure here (oceanfactoryfloor-{1,2,3}, warm-up discarded), using leg-diff's OWN loader -- the basis that will apply it. CV 2.751%, mean 307.0 us/frame, n=3. THE METHOD WAS VALIDATED BEFORE THE NEW NUMBER WAS TAKEN: recomputing the recorded floors from those legs reproduces lighting.produce.entities.us, cpu.frame.render.us, lighting.cpu.total.us and cpu.frame.total.us to three decimals. THE UNION IS FAR STEADIER THAN ITS LARGEST MEMBER -- 2.751% against lighting.cpu.total.us's 13.952% -- which is expected and is an argument for using it as the denominator: summing seven members averages away per-member variance that a single part carries alone.
_basis: EVERY FIGURE IN THIS FILE IS THE COEFFICIENT OF VARIATION, ACROSS LEGS, OF total/frames -- the metric's summed microseconds divided by the leg's frame count, where frames is cpu.frame.total.us's count. THAT IS THE CONSUMER'S BASIS: leg-diff.py computes exactly this per leg and compares the results, so a floor derived any other way is a bar from a different measurement. The alternative that actually bit us is per-CALL (total/count), which for a key whose count is not the frame count is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY, not a rescaling -- and CV does not survive it. scripts/ci/floor-reproduces.py re-derives every entry below from its own banked legs on this basis and fails if any disagrees, so this declaration is enforced rather than asserted.
_four_floors_did_not_reproduce: AND MY FILED EXPLANATION FOR IT WAS WRONG. [#285] recorded that two 04-Ocean-Factory floors did not reproduce and blamed telemetry-window's COVERAGE-SCALED basis, on a cadence correlation of 4-for-4 and 2-for-2 at one scene. Re-deriving all six scenes refutes that twice over. (1) CADENCE IS NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR: the same two call-cadence keys reproduce EXACTLY at Desert-Town, 00-Ocean-Lab, 01-Lava-Refinery and 03-Surface-Outpost, so the pattern is 2-for-12, not 2-for-2. (2) COVERAGE VARIATION IS NOT THE DISCRIMINATOR EITHER, and points the wrong way: the two scenes that fail have the STEADIEST coverage of all six (0.185% and 0.155%), while 03-Surface-Outpost swings 91.84/99.96/39.81% -- 42% -- and reproduces to three decimals. THE ACTUAL CAUSE, established 4-for-4 by trying each candidate basis against the recorded number: those floors were derived PER CALL (total/count) while leg-diff applies them PER FRAME (total/frames). Confirmed in the other direction too, 8-for-8: at the four scenes that reproduce, per-frame matches the record and per-call does not -- at 03-Surface-Outpost by a factor of four (46.446 vs 11.259). So this table was populated by TWO DIFFERENT DERIVATIONS and recorded neither. It was never a property of the keys; it was two people-shaped passes over one file, which is why no rule about cadence or coverage could predict it. FIXED HERE: 04-Ocean-Factory cpu_cost 3.613 -> 3.735 and drive.point 3.814 -> 3.912; ship cpu_cost 7.427 -> 7.561 and drive.point 7.086 -> 7.211. All four move UP, so every verdict they gated was too permissive, never too strict. The union figure was unaffected -- it was measured on leg-diff's basis deliberately.

_banks._what: The legs each floor was derived from, as DATA rather than prose, so scripts/ci/floor-reproduces.py can re-derive and check rather than take the provenance's word. Paths are relative to harness/profiles/ and omit the .json. WARM-UP LEGS ARE NOT LISTED because they were discarded before derivation; a bank is the legs that produced the number, not the legs that were run.
_banks._scene_attribution: The four stab-* banks predate the profiler recording meta.scene, so their artefacts do NOT self-describe their place and the scene attribution rests on the FILENAME. The gate therefore cannot verify their scene, only re-derive their numbers. The oceanfactoryfloor-*, shipfloor-* and walkfloor-* banks do carry meta.scene, and the gate asserts it matches.

_absent_is_not_zero: A key or scene NOT listed here has NO MEASURED FLOOR. leg-diff.py refuses to attribute rather than assuming zero, because an unmeasured floor and a floor of zero produce opposite verdicts from the same data.
